messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

input.rationale: The agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant. Searches for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel" and a sweep of all "shall not" obligations return only (i) confidentiality duties, (ii) the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture clause referring to "employee" only as a relationship descriptor (p0061), and (iii) the Section 6 exclusivity covenants, which restrict participation in competing Internet projects (p0037 on the Company, p0042 on HDI) rather than the hiring or solicitation of either party's staff. Because no hiring restriction is imposed on us as Customer, the preferred position — no non-solicit on Customer — is already satisfied and no redline is required. Note for the deal team: the exclusivity covenant at p0037 binds us during the term, but that is a competition restriction reviewed under a separate rule, not within the scope of NOSOLICIT.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

payload.sectionRef: § SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT

paragraphs.text: SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT

This SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT (the "Agreement") dated as of August 9, 1999 is made between Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI"), a New Jersey Corporation, located at 1500 Harbor Boulevard, Weehawken, NJ 07087, and The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company"), a Nevada corporation, located at 2500 Arrowhead Drive, Carson City, NV 89706. Each of the parties hereto shall be referred to as a "Party".
In consideration of the mutual promises and covenants set forth below, HDI and the Company agree as follows:
1. HDI's Responsibilities.

1.1 HDI shall design, develop, implement, operate, maintain and manage, and enable the Company to establish a presence on the World Wide Web ("Site") to make available to Internet users on demand, men's and women's apparel and accessories from the Deerskin Catalog ("Deerskin Products"). As used in this Agreement, "Deerskin Products" shall not include (i) closeout merchandise which the Company may identify as "Deerskin" branded items, if such is the case, nor (ii) products from the Company's Joan Cook Catalog.
1.2 HDI shall bear all costs associated with the design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance and management of the Site, including, without limitation, technology and labor.
1.3 HDI shall host and maintain the Site on a server provided by HDI.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

input.summary: Add a mutual liability cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims and a mutual consequential-damages exclusion.
input.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no limitation of liability, leaving both Parties exposed to unlimited and consequential damages, so we have added our standard mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000. Confidentiality, data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement claims sit outside the cap, and the Company's payment obligations are not treated as damages; a straight twelve months' fees cap is our fallback.

ops.text: 10.9 Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, (a) neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, or for lost profits or lost revenues, arising out of or relating to this Agreement; and (b) each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (ii) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000). Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement obligation on us. I confirmed this by searching for each detection trigger ("solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel") and by sweeping every "shall not" obligation in the document. The only hits were:

- **p0061** (No Joint Venture) — uses "employee" merely to describe the relationship between the parties, not as a hiring restriction.
- **p0048–p0054** — confidentiality duties.
- **p0037 / p0042** (Section 6, Exclusivity) — restrict participation in competing Internet projects, not the solicitation or hiring of either party's staff.

Since the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer) is already achieved, no edit was needed.

One flag for the deal team, outside this rule's scope: the exclusivity covenant at **p0037** does bind us (the Company) during the term, barring participation in projects similar to the Site for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products. Note the asymmetry — HDI's mirror covenant at **p0042** runs for the term *plus two years* post-expiration and survives under Section 10.7, whereas ours is term-only. That favors us, but the restriction on us should still be reviewed under whichever non-compete/exclusivity rule covers competitive covenants.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant. **Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

- **No MFN burdening us.** Searches for "most favo(u)red", "favorable/favourable", "best", "lowest", "third party", and the fee provisions turned up no obligation for The Deerskin Companies to give HDI terms no less favourable than those given to others, or to match third-party offers.
- **Fees are fixed, not MFN-linked.** Section 3.1 sets a flat 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month, with no benchmarking or true-up against third-party arrangements.
- **The one "no less favorably" clause runs in our favour.** Section 1.8 requires *HDI* to promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favorably than its own catalog titles — a vendor-side benefit we keep untouched per the redline guidance.
- **Section 6.1 noted but out of scope.** It is an exclusivity/non-participation covenant on us, not a most-favoured-nation obligation; it would fall under an exclusivity rule rather than MFN.

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or best-terms obligation running against us. The fee provisions (Sections 3.1–3.4) set a flat 30% of Net Sales above a monthly threshold with no obligation for the Company to extend HDI any better terms given to third parties, and Section 6.1 is an exclusivity/non-compete covenant rather than an MFN. The only "no less favorably" language, Section 1.8, runs in our favour: HDI must promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favorably than its own catalog titles. Consistent with the playbook, a Vendor-granted MFN-style benefit is welcome and is not redlined.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

input.rationale: The agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant. Searches for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel" and a sweep of all "shall not" obligations return only (i) confidentiality duties, (ii) the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture clause referring to "employee" only as a relationship descriptor (p0061), and (iii) the Section 6 exclusivity covenants, which restrict participation in competing Internet projects (p0037 on the Company, p0042 on HDI) rather than the hiring or solicitation of either party's staff. Because no hiring restriction is imposed on us as Customer, the preferred position — no non-solicit on Customer — is already satisfied and no redline is required. Note for the deal team: the exclusivity covenant at p0037 binds us during the term, but that is a competition restriction reviewed under a separate rule, not within the scope of NOSOLICIT.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement obligation on us. I confirmed this by searching for each detection trigger ("solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel") and by sweeping every "shall not" obligation in the document. The only hits were:

- **p0061** (No Joint Venture) — uses "employee" merely to describe the relationship between the parties, not as a hiring restriction.
- **p0048–p0054** — confidentiality duties.
- **p0037 / p0042** (Section 6, Exclusivity) — restrict participation in competing Internet projects, not the solicitation or hiring of either party's staff.

Since the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer) is already achieved, no edit was needed.

One flag for the deal team, outside this rule's scope: the exclusivity covenant at **p0037** does bind us (the Company) during the term, barring participation in projects similar to the Site for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products. Note the asymmetry — HDI's mirror covenant at **p0042** runs for the term *plus two years* post-expiration and survives under Section 10.7, whereas ours is term-only. That favors us, but the restriction on us should still be reviewed under whichever non-compete/exclusivity rule covers competitive covenants.

Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

input.rationale: The Agreement has no limitation-of-liability, damages-exclusion or aggregate-liability language anywhere: Section 9 (Warranties) contains only corporate/authority representations, Section 10 (General Provisions) covers notices through headings, and the only uses of "liability" (Sections 10.2) are agency/partnership disclaimers. There is also no indemnity clause. Both Parties are therefore exposed to unlimited direct and consequential damages, which fails the required mutual cap. We added a new Section 10.9 in General Provisions (which survives under the existing survival clause) imposing a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees payable by the Company under Section 3 and USD 1,000,000, a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, uncapped Excluded Claims for confidentiality, data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmation that the Company's payment and Termination Payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual liability cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims and a mutual consequential-damages exclusion.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no limitation of liability, leaving both Parties exposed to unlimited and consequential damages, so we have added our standard mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000. Confidentiality, data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement claims sit outside the cap, and the Company's payment obligations are not treated as damages; a straight twelve months' fees cap is our fallback.

ops.text: 10.9 Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, (a) neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, or for lost profits or lost revenues, arising out of or relating to this Agreement; and (b) each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (ii) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000). "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. The Company's obligations to make payments under Section 3 and any Termination Payment shall not be treated as damages for purposes of this Section 10.9.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
input.rationale: Section 6.1 imposes an exclusive dealing obligation on us (the Company): for the entire term we may not participate in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or the broad set of "substantially similar" products, and HDI gets the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand online. Because Section 4.1 renews the term automatically each year on 90 days' notice, and early termination by us triggers a Termination Payment under Section 4.2, this is effectively exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit — the walk-away position. HDI's reciprocal covenant in Section 6.3 and the closeout carve-out in Section 6.2 benefit us and are left untouched. Given the reciprocal bargain and HDI's development/hosting investment, we took the fallback: exclusivity confined to Deerskin Products for a fixed 12 months, terminating automatically on HDI's failure to meet service levels, availability requirements or delivery dates (including the Section 1.6 launch date).

proposal.summary: Narrow Section 6.1 exclusivity binding the Company to Deerskin Products for 12 months, with automatic termination on HDI performance failure
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we should not be subject to an exclusivity or sole-source commitment, so we have narrowed Section 6.1 to Deerskin Products for a fixed twelve (12) month period rather than the full rolling term, and made it fall away automatically if HDI misses its service levels or delivery dates. HDI's reciprocal covenant in Section 6.3 is unchanged.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Position — walk-away:
Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.
Detection guidance:
Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

content.text:
**Finding: MISSING (critical) — no limitation of liability in the Agreement.**

Investigation summary:
- **Full-text scan** for "liability", "damages", "consequential", "aggregate", "exceed", "no event", "limitation" returned no cap or damages-exclusion language. The only hits on "liability" (Section 10.2, p0061–p0062) are no-joint-venture/agency disclaimers.
- **Section 9 (Warranties)** contains only entity/authority representations plus a Globix carve-out — no liability language hidden there.
- **Section 10 (General Provisions)** runs notices → headings with no cap; there is **no indemnity clause** at all.
- **Fee basis check:** Section 3.1 — the Company pays HDI 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month, so "fees paid or payable by the Company" is a real, non-illusory cap base (and Section 2 contemplates a Termination Payment tied to twelve months' Net Sales).

Both Parties are exposed to unlimited direct and consequential damages, so the preferred position is proposed rather than a fallback.

Redline (validated `ok:true`) — new **Section 10.9** inserted after 10.8, which survives for two years under the existing Section 10.7 survival clause:
- Mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential/punitive damages and lost profits;
- Mutual cap at the **greater of twelve months' fees payable by the Company and USD 1,000,000**;
- **Uncapped Excluded Claims**: confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP;
- The Company's Section 3 payments and any Termination Payment are expressly **not "damages"** for cap purposes, so the cap cannot be used to erode HDI's payment entitlement or ours.

Placement in General Provisions (rather than a new numbered section after Warranties) avoids renumbering Section 10 and keeps the edit minimal.

messages.content:
Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
The Agreement has no limitation-of-liability, damages-exclusion or aggregate-liability language anywhere: Section 9 (Warranties) contains only corporate/authority representations, Section 10 (General Provisions) covers notices through headings, and the only uses of "liability" (Sections 10.2) are agency/partnership disclaimers. There is also no indemnity clause. Both Parties are therefore exposed to unlimited direct and consequential damages, which fails the required mutual cap. We added a new Section 10.9 in General Provisions (which survives under the existing survival clause) imposing a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees payable by the Company under Section 3 and USD 1,000,000, a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, uncapped Excluded Claims for confidentiality, data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmation that the Company's payment and Termination Payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Original paragraphs:
p0059: 10. General Provisions.
p0070: 10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement. This Agreement is being executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but all of which shall constitute one and the same instrument.

Resolved definitions:
none

Rendered redline:
p0070: 10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement. This Agreement is being executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but all of which shall constitute one and the same instrument.
10.9 Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, (a) neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages, or for lost profits or lost revenues, arising out of or relating to this Agreement; and (b) each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (ii) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000). "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. The Company's obligations to make payments under Section 3 and any Termination Payment shall not be treated as damages for purposes of this Section 10.9.

Comment:
[Playbook] The Agreement contains no limitation of liability, leaving both Parties exposed to unlimited and consequential damages, so we have added our standard mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000. Confidentiality, data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement claims sit outside the cap, and the Company's payment obligations are not treated as damages; a straight twelve months' fees cap is our fallback.

input.rationale: The Agreement contains no indemnification, defence or hold-harmless language anywhere (searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless" and "liability" return only the no-joint-venture clause), and no limitation of liability. input.summary: Add HDI (vendor) indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, HDI-caused data incidents and misconduct
input.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no indemnity at all, so we have added an HDI indemnity covering third-party IP infringement claims relating to the Site and HDI's services, HDI's breach of law, HDI-caused data incidents and HDI's gross negligence or willful misconduct, with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics. HDI builds, hosts and operates the Site, so it should stand behind claims arising from what it delivers; we can discuss customary IP exclusions (Company Content, Marks, specifications and modifications) if helpful.

ops.text: Indemnification by HDI. HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, losses, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (1) an allegation that the Site, the services performed by HDI hereunder or any software, systems or materials provided by HDI (excluding Content or Marks provided by the Company) infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (2) HDI's breach of applicable law; (3) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Content, Confidential Information or customer or user data caused by HDI; or (4) HDI's gross negligence or willful misconduct. The Company shall promptly notify HDI of any such claim, HDI shall have control of the defense and settlement thereof (provided that no settlement imposing any liability, obligation or admission on the Company shall be entered into without the Company's prior written consent), and the Company shall provide reasonable cooperation at HDI's expense.

input.quote: 9. Warranties.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no indemnification, defence or hold-harmless language anywhere (searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless" and "liability" return only the no-joint-venture clause), and no limitation of liability. HDI is the vendor: it designs, develops, hosts, operates and promotes the Site (Sections 1.1-1.8) and performs "Services" for the Company (Section 8.1), yet bears no obligation to defend the Company against third-party claims, including IP infringement claims arising from the Site, HDI's software/systems or HDI's promotional activity (Section 7.2 only contains a covenant, with no indemnity). This fails the preferred position, so we insert a vendor indemnity as new Section 9(c), immediately after the warranty section and before General Provisions; it will survive under Section 10.7 (which preserves Section 9). Customer-side exposure is limited by carving out Company-provided Content and Marks; no Company indemnity is added.

input.quote: 10.2 No Joint Venture. The Parties agree that and acknowledge that the relationship of the Parties is in the nature of an independent contractor. This Agreement shall not be deemed to create a partnership or joint venture and neither Party is the other's agent, partner, employee or representative.
input.rationale:
No non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant exists anywhere in this Agreement, so the preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer") is already met and no redline is required.

Basis for absence: searches for each detection trigger ("solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel") plus a full sweep of every "shall not" obligation returned only three categories of text, none of which restricts hiring: (i) p0061, quoted above, where "employee" appears solely as a relationship descriptor in the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture clause; (ii) the confidentiality duties at p0048-p0054, which restrict use and disclosure of information, not recruitment of staff; and (iii) the Section 6 exclusivity covenants, which restrict participation in competing Internet projects for Deerskin Products (p0037 binding the Company, p0042 binding HDI) rather than the solicitation or hiring of either party's employees.

On the two failed deterministic checks (12-month duration and general-solicitation carve-out): these are not defects. Both test attributes that can only exist inside a non-solicit clause. Because there is no such clause, there is no duration to shorten and no carve-out to add. Inserting a carve-out sentence would require first drafting the restrictive covenant it qualifies, which would import a restriction on us that the counterparty never asked for and move us away from the preferred position. The correct outcome under this rule is therefore no edit, and the rendered paragraphs remain byte-identical to the originals.

Separate note for the deal team, outside NOSOLICIT scope: the exclusivity covenant at p0037 does bind us during the term, and it is asymmetric in our favour only as to duration - HDI's mirror covenant at p0042 runs for the term plus two years and survives under Section 10.7, while ours is term-only. That competition restriction should be reviewed under the applicable exclusivity/non-compete rule.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence

No non-solicit on Customer.

Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.

"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Searches for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel" and a sweep of all "shall not" obligations return only (i) confidentiality duties, (ii) the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture clause referring to "employee" only as a relationship descriptor (p0061), and (iii) the Section 6 exclusivity covenants, which restrict participation in competing Internet projects (p0037 on the Company, p0042 on HDI) rather than the hiring or solicitation of either party's staff. Because no hiring restriction is imposed on us as Customer, the preferred position — no non-solicit on Customer — is already satisfied and no redline is required. content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement obligation on us. I confirmed this by searching for each detection trigger ("solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel") and by sweeping every "shall not" obligation in the document. The only hits were:

- **p0061** (No Joint Venture) — uses "employee" merely to describe the relationship between the parties, not as a hiring restriction.
- **p0048–p0054** — confidentiality duties.
- **p0037 / p0042** (Section 6, Exclusivity) — restrict participation in competing Internet projects, not the solicitation or hiring of either party's staff.

Since the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer) is already achieved, no edit was needed.

One flag for the deal team, outside this rule's scope: the exclusivity covenant at **p0037** does bind us (the Company) during the term, barring participation in projects similar to the Site for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products. Note the asymmetry — HDI's mirror covenant at **p0042** runs for the term *plus two years* post-expiration and survives under Section 10.7, whereas ours is term-only. That favors us, but the restriction on us should still be reviewed under whichever non-compete/exclusivity rule covers competitive covenants.

input.rationale:
No non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant exists anywhere in this Agreement, so the preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer") is already met and no redline is required.

Basis for absence: searches for each detection trigger ("solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel") plus a full sweep of every "shall not" obligation returned only three categories of text, none of which restricts hiring: (i) p0061, quoted above, where "employee" appears solely as a relationship descriptor in the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture clause; (ii) the confidentiality duties at p0048-p0054, which restrict use and disclosure of information, not recruitment of staff; and (iii) the Section 6 exclusivity covenants, which restrict participation in competing Internet projects for Deerskin Products (p0037 binding the Company, p0042 binding HDI) rather than the solicitation or hiring of either party's employees.

On the two failed deterministic checks (12-month duration and general-solicitation carve-out): these are not defects. Both test attributes that can only exist inside a non-solicit clause. Because there is no such clause, there is no duration to shorten and no carve-out to add. Inserting a carve-out sentence would require first drafting the restrictive covenant it qualifies, which would import a restriction on us that the counterparty never asked for and move us away from the preferred position. The correct outcome under this rule is therefore no edit, and the rendered paragraphs remain byte-identical to the originals.

Separate note for the deal team, outside NOSOLICIT scope: the exclusivity covenant at p0037 does bind us during the term, and it is asymmetric in our favour only as to duration - HDI's mirror covenant at p0042 runs for the term plus two years and survives under Section 10.7, while ours is term-only. That competition restriction should be reviewed under the applicable exclusivity/non-compete rule.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.rationale: Section 6.1 imposes a field-of-use / non-compete restriction on the Company (our party): during the term it may not participate in any similar Internet project with respect to Deerskin Products "or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products," expressly sweeping in third-party competitor lines (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and "companies similar" to them). That is an open-ended limit on the products we may source, build or sell online, with no carve-out for internal development or acquired businesses. The reciprocal restriction on HDI in Section 6.3 is acceptable (it binds the vendor). Because HDI funds the Site and the Deerskin-brand exclusivity is the core bargain, we took the fallback rather than outright deletion: the restriction is limited to a self-contained "Deerskin" branded consumer web site, remains term-only (Section 4.1 term is one year with annual renewals terminable on 90 days' notice, so no post-term tail), and carve-outs for other channels, internal development and acquisitions are added.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

content.text:
**Finding: MISSING (critical) — no indemnification anywhere in the Agreement.**

- Searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless" and "infring" turned up nothing indemnity-related; the only "liability" hits are the no-joint-venture clause (§10.2). There is also no limitation of liability.
- HDI is clearly the vendor (designs, develops, hosts, operates, maintains and promotes the Site under §§1.1–1.8; performs "Services" per §8.1), and the Company retains editorial control and supplies Content and Marks — yet HDI has no duty to defend the Company against third-party claims, including IP infringement claims arising from the Site, HDI's software/systems, or HDI's cross-promotions (§7.2 is a bare covenant with no indemnity).

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** new §9(c) inserted after p0058 — i.e., at the end of Warranties and immediately before General Provisions — giving the Company and its affiliates a defence/indemnity for (1) IP infringement allegations regarding the Site, HDI's services and HDI-provided software/systems (carving out Company Content and Marks), (2) HDI's breach of law, (3) HDI-caused unauthorised access to Content/Confidential Information/user data, and (4) HDI's gross negligence or willful misconduct, with standard notice, control-of-defence (no adverse settlement without consent) and cooperation mechanics. **Finding submitted: deviation (high severity), Section 6.1 (¶p0037).**

**What I found**

Section 6 ("Exclusivity") contains two covenants pointing in opposite directions:

- **§6.1 binds us.** For the *entire term* we may not participate in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products — or for the sweeping open-ended category of "products substantially similar," which pulls in Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and unnamed "companies similar" to them — and HDI receives the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand online.
- **§6.3 binds HDI** (no similar projects during the term plus two years) and **§6.2** preserves our closeout-merchandise site. Both benefit us, so I left them untouched.

**Why this hits the walk-away line.** §4.1 renews the term automatically each anniversary, and §4.2 makes our own termination expensive (a Termination Payment keyed to trailing twelve-month Net Sales less $800,000, halved). So the restriction is indefinite in practice and our only exit is a paid one. The single performance hook, §1.6, expires 70 days after signature — after launch, HDI can underperform indefinitely while we stay locked up.

**Position taken: fallback, not preferred.** Outright deletion would be disproportionate here — this is a genuinely reciprocal bargain, with HDI funding development and hosting and giving up a two-year post-term covenant of its own. I therefore narrowed rather than struck:

1. Term cut from the rolling agreement term to a fixed **twelve (12) months** from the Effective Date.
2. Scope confined to **Deerskin Products**, deleting the elastic "substantially similar"/named-competitor extension.
3. Added **automatic termination** of the restriction on any HDI failure to meet service levels, availability requirements or delivery dates, including §1.6.

The redline validated `ok:true` before submission. Confidence 0.86 — the detection and direction are unambiguous; the residual uncertainty is only whether the business will accept the fallback or push for full deletion, given HDI's §6.3 covenant is the consideration on the other side of this trade.

Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.

Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant exists anywhere in this Agreement, so the preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer") is already met and no redline is required.

Basis for absence: searches for each detection trigger ("solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel") plus a full sweep of every "shall not" obligation returned only three categories of text, none of which restricts hiring: (i) p0061, quoted above, where "employee" appears solely as a relationship descriptor in the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture clause; (ii) the confidentiality duties at p0048-p0054, which restrict use and disclosure of information, not recruitment of staff; and (iii) the Section 6 exclusivity covenants, which restrict participation in competing Internet projects for Deerskin Products (p0037 binding the Company, p0042 binding HDI) rather than the solicitation or hiring of either party's employees.

On the two failed deterministic checks (12-month duration and general-solicitation carve-out): these are not defects. Both test attributes that can only exist inside a non-solicit clause. Because there is no such clause, there is no duration to shorten and no carve-out to add. Inserting a carve-out sentence would require first drafting the restrictive covenant it qualifies, which would import a restriction on us that the counterparty never asked for and move us away from the preferred position. The correct outcome under this rule is therefore no edit, and the rendered paragraphs remain byte-identical to the originals.

Separate note for the deal team, outside NOSOLICIT scope: the exclusivity covenant at p0037 does bind us during the term, and it is asymmetric in our favour only as to duration - HDI's mirror covenant at p0042 runs for the term plus two years and survives under Section 10.7, while ours is term-only. That competition restriction should be reviewed under the applicable exclusivity/non-compete rule.

**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 6.1 (¶ p0037)**

Contrary to the planner's "likely absent" hint, the agreement does contain a restrictive covenant binding us. Section 6.1 bars the Company, during the term, from participating in *any* similar Internet project involving Deerskin Products "or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products," expressly including third-party competitor lines (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled, and "companies similar" to them) — an undefined field-of-use restriction on what we may source, build or sell, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions.

Notes on direction and proportionality:
- Section 6.3 (two-year post-term restriction on HDI) binds the vendor and was left untouched.
- Section 6.2 (closeout-merchandise site) is a limited existing carve-out benefiting us.
- Because HDI bears all Site development and hosting costs and the "Deerskin"-brand exclusivity is the core bargain, I took the **fallback** rather than deleting the covenant: the restriction is confined to a self-contained "Deerskin"-branded consumer web site, stays term-only (Section 4.1 — one year, annual renewals, 90 days' notice, so no post-term tail), and gains carve-outs for other channels, internal development and acquired businesses.

Redline validated (ok:true) and finding submitted with the [Playbook]-prefixed comment offering deletion as our preferred position.

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 6.1 imposes a field-of-use / non-compete restriction on the Company (our party): during the term it may not participate in any similar Internet project with respect to Deerskin Products "or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products," expressly sweeping in third-party competitor lines (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and "companies similar" to them). That is an open-ended limit on the products we may source, build or sell online, with no carve-out for internal development or acquired businesses. The reciprocal restriction on HDI in Section 6.3 is acceptable (it binds the vendor). Because HDI funds the Site and the Deerskin-brand exclusivity is the core bargain, we took the fallback rather than outright deletion: the restriction is limited to a self-contained "Deerskin" branded consumer web site, remains term-only (Section 4.1 term is one year with annual renewals terminable on 90 days' notice, so no post-term tail), and carve-outs for other channels, internal development and acquisitions are added.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement obligation on us. I confirmed this by searching for each detection trigger ("solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel") and by sweeping every "shall not" obligation in the document. The only hits were:

- **p0061** (No Joint Venture) — uses "employee" merely to describe the relationship between the parties, not as a hiring restriction.
- **p0048–p0054** — confidentiality duties.
- **p0037 / p0042** (Section 6, Exclusivity) — restrict participation in competing Internet projects, not the solicitation or hiring of either party's staff.

Since the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer) is already achieved, no edit was needed.

One flag for the deal team, outside this rule's scope: the exclusivity covenant at **p0037** does bind us (the Company) during the term, barring participation in projects similar to the Site for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products. Note the asymmetry — HDI's mirror covenant at **p0042** runs for the term *plus two years* post-expiration and survives under Section 10.7, whereas ours is term-only. That favors us, but the restriction on us should still be reviewed under whichever non-compete/exclusivity rule covers competitive covenants.

ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.

Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.

Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.

Non-renewal notice windows longer than 90 days, or automatic multi-year renewals.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Redline guidance:
Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

content.text: The verifier's feedback this round affirms every substantive element: status, cited text, party mapping, the absence of a redline, byte-identical paragraphs, and the out-of-scope exclusivity note. The sole failing check — general-solicitation carve-out — is expressly characterized as non-probative and consistent with absence rather than a defect. There is no substantive defect left to repair, and manufacturing a carve-out to satisfy the check would require drafting the very restriction the rule tells us to avoid. I'll resubmit the finding unchanged in substance.

input.quote: 10.2 No Joint Venture. The Parties agree that and acknowledge that the relationship of the Parties is in the nature of an independent contractor. This Agreement shall not be deemed to create a partnership or joint venture and neither Party is the other's agent, partner, employee or representative.
input.rationale:
No non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant exists anywhere in this Agreement, so the preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer") is already met and no redline is required.

Basis for absence: searches for each detection trigger ("solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel") plus a sweep of every "shall not" obligation returned only three categories of text, none of which restricts hiring: (i) p0061, quoted above, where "employee" appears solely as a relationship descriptor in the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture clause; (ii) the confidentiality duties at p0048-p0054, which restrict use and disclosure of information, not recruitment of staff; and (iii) the Section 6 exclusivity covenants, which restrict participation in competing Internet projects for Deerskin Products (p0037 binding the Company, p0042 binding HDI) rather than solicitation or hiring of either party's employees.

Party mapping: our client, The Deerskin Companies, Inc. ("the Company"), is the customer under this site development and hosting agreement; HDI is the vendor/host. The rule's concern is a covenant binding Customer, and none exists.

On the outstanding "general-solicitation carve-out" check: this is not a defect and cannot be cured. The check tests an attribute that can only exist inside a non-solicit clause, as does the companion 12-month duration check. With no such clause in the document, there is no duration to shorten and no carve-out to attach. Drafting a carve-out would require first drafting the restrictive covenant it qualifies, importing a personnel restriction on us that the counterparty never sought and moving us away from the preferred position. The correct outcome is therefore no edit, and the rendered paragraphs remain byte-identical to the originals.

Separate note for the deal team, outside NOSOLICIT scope: the exclusivity covenant at p0037 does bind us during the term, and is asymmetric in our favour only as to duration - HDI's mirror covenant at p0042 runs for the term plus two years and survives under Section 10.7, while ours is term-only. That competition restriction should be reviewed under the applicable exclusivity/non-compete rule.

Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Rule:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback.
