payload.sectionRef: § 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a

paragraphs.text: 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a

General Manager of its own to act as liaison with the other Party for the Site (each a "General Manager") who shall bear sole responsibility for bookkeeping and business operations of the Site on a day-today basis. Each General Manager shall have the authority to make and convey decisions on behalf of each Party and to be the liaison with the other Party for all production and Content matters.
6. Exclusivity.

6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
The Company hereby grants to HDI a non-exclusive, limited, non-transferable license to use the Company's "Deerskin" trademarks, service

marks, and logos (collectively, "Marks") solely for the purpose of carrying out its obligations under this Agreement. Except as provided herein, no licenses of the Company's Marks are granted or implied under this Agreement.
6.2 The Company retains the right to establish a web site on the Internet for the purpose of offering closeout
merchandise which may be identified as "Deerskin" branded products, if such is the case.

6.3 During the term of this Agreement and for a period of two years after the expiration date of this Agreement, HDI shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet from which products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) are offered for sale to consumers on the Internet.
7. Cross-Promotions.

7.1 Joint Efforts. The Parties agree to cross-promote one another's products through the use of their respective customer e-mail lists on a reciprocal and equitable basis. The Parties specifically agree that the form, content and design of any and all advertisements or promotional materials featuring the other Party or such Party's products shall continue to be developed by or on behalf of such Party and shall be subject to such Party's final approval. The Parties agree further that any promotions or advertisements involving the use of a Party's customer e-mail list by the other Party shall be subject to the prior approval of such Party.

7.2 Mutual Covenants as to Advertisements. The Parties hereby covenant and agree that their respective marketing and advertising efforts provided for herein shall at all times comply with all applicable laws rules and regulations and will

not contain any material which is obscene, threatening, fraudulent, harassing, libelous, infringing of third party intellectual property rights, otherwise illegal or, in the reasonable judgment of the Party required to display or transmit the advertisement, offensive.
8. Confidentiality.

8.1 Unless otherwise agreed to in writing by the Company, HDI shall maintain the strict confidentiality and shall not disclose to any third party the existence of, or terms and conditions of this Agreement. In addition, HDI, in performing the Services for the Company hereunder, may have access to or be exposed to, directly or indirectly, Content, user information, data, knowledge and proprietary and trade secret information of the Company in oral, graphic, written, electronic or machine readable form (hereinafter collectively referred to as "Confidential Information"). Confidential Information shall not include information which can be demonstrated:
(a) to have been rightfully in the possession of HDI from a source other than the Company prior to the time of disclosure of said information to HDI hereunder ("Time of Receipt");
(b) to have been in the public domain prior to the Time of Receipt;

(c) to have become part of the public domain after the Time of Receipt by a publication or by any other means except an unauthorized act or omission or breach of this Agreement on the part of HDI, its employees, or agents; or (d) to have been supplied to HDI after the Time of Receipt by a third party who is under no obligation to the
Company to maintain such information in confidence.

8.2 HDI Obligations. All Confidential Information of the Company shall be held in strict confidence by HDI and shall not be disclosed or used without express written consent of the Company, except as may be required by law. HDI shall use reasonable measures and reasonable efforts to provide protection for Confidential Information, including measures at least as strict as those HDI uses to protect its own Confidential Information.

8.3 Company's Obligations. The Company acknowledges that it may receive confidential information of HDI relating to its technical, marketing, product and/or business affairs. All such confidential information of HDI shall be-held in strict confidence by the Company and shall not be disclosed or used without express written consent of HDI, except as may be required by law. The Company shall use reasonable measures and reasonable efforts to provide protection for such confidential information of HDI, including measures at least as strict as those the Company uses to protect its own Confidential Information.
9. Warranties.

(a) Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party that (1) it is a corporation organized, validly existing and in goodstanding under the laws of the state of its incorporation; (2) it has the full right power and authority to enter into, and to perform the obligations contemplated in this Agreement, and the person signing on its behalf has the full right,

power and authority to enter into this Agreement on behalf of the Party; (3) this Agreement constitutes a legal valid and binding obligation of the Party, enforceable in accordance with its terms; and (4) the execution of this Agreement will not conflict in any way with any pre-existing agreements or understandings of the Party with any person or entity.

(b) HDI acknowledges that the Company is currently a party to a web-hosting agreement with Globix Corporation (the "Globix Agreement") for the Company's web site offering Deerskin Products to Internet customers. HDI agrees that the Company shall not be deemed in breach of any provision of this Agreement by virtue of the Globix Agreement remaining in effect after this Agreement has been executed by both Parties, provided, that the Globix Agreement is terminated on or prior to the Effective Date
10. General Provisions.

10.1 Notices. Any notice under this Agreement will be in writing and delivered by personal delivery, express courier, confirmed facsimile, or certified or registered mail, return receipt requested and will be deemed given upon personal delivery, one (1) day after deposit with express courier, upon confirmation of receipt of facsimile or five (5),days after deposit in the mail. Notices will be sent to a Party at its address set forth above or such other address as that Party may specify in writing pursuant to this Section.

10.2 No Joint Venture. The Parties agree that and acknowledge that the relationship of the Parties is in the nature of an independent contractor. This Agreement shall not be deemed to create a partnership or joint venture and neither Party is the other's agent, partner, employee or representative. Neither Party shall have any right, power or authority to enter into any agreement for or on behalf of, or to assume or create any obligation, liability, or responsibility on behalf of the other.

This Agreement will not be construed to create or imply an association, joint venture, co-ownership, or partnership between the Parties or to impose any partnership obligation or liability upon either Party.

10.3 Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.

10.4 Waiver of Breach. The failure of either Party at any time to enforce any of the provisions of this Agreement shall not be deemed or construed to be a waiver of any such provisions, or in any way to affect the right of any Party hereto to thereafter enforce each and every provision of this Agreement. No waiver of any breach of any provisions of this Agreement shall be effective unless set forth in writing and executed by the Party against which enforcement of such waiver is sought; and no waiver of any such breach shall be construed or deemed to be a waiver of any other or subsequent breach.

10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
10.6 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is declared invalid or otherwise determined to be unenforceable
for any reason, such provision shall be deemed to be severable from the remaining provisions of this Agreement, which shall otherwise remain in full force and effect.
10.7 Survival. Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 of this Agreement shall survive and continue in full force and effect for a period of two years from the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

10.7 Entire Agreement. This Agreement is the complete and exclusive agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, superseding any prior agreements and communications (both written and oral) regarding such subject matter. This Agreement may only be modified, or any rights under it waived, by a written document executed by both Parties.

10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement. This Agreement is being executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but all of which shall constitute one and the same instrument.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have duly executed this Agreement as of the date first above written.

payload.sectionRef: § SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT

paragraphs.text: SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT

This SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT (the "Agreement") dated as of August 9, 1999 is made between Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI"), a New Jersey Corporation, located at 1500 Harbor Boulevard, Weehawken, NJ 07087, and The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company"), a Nevada corporation, located at 2500 Arrowhead Drive, Carson City, NV 89706. Each of the parties hereto shall be referred to as a "Party".
In consideration of the mutual promises and covenants set forth below, HDI and the Company agree as follows:
1. HDI's Responsibilities.

1.1 HDI shall design, develop, implement, operate, maintain and manage, and enable the Company to establish a presence on the World Wide Web ("Site") to make available to Internet users on demand, men's and women's apparel and accessories from the Deerskin Catalog ("Deerskin Products"). As used in this Agreement, "Deerskin Products" shall not include (i) closeout merchandise which the Company may identify as "Deerskin" branded items, if such is the case, nor (ii) products from the Company's Joan Cook Catalog.
1.2 HDI shall bear all costs associated with the design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance and management of the Site, including, without limitation, technology and labor.
1.3 HDI shall host and maintain the Site on a server provided by HDI.

Severity: medium
Category: commercial

No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.

Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Insert Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide transition assistance, return Company data in machine-readable format within 30 days, and certify deletion.
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 4 sets out termination mechanics and the Termination Payment but says nothing about winding down the hosted Site, so we have added an exit clause requiring HDI to return the Company's Content, user, customer and order data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, provide up to six (6) months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, and certify deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety (90) days of assistance with the same thirty-day data export.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site and its operations to the Company or its designee; (b) within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer data, order data and other Confidential Information of the Company then in HDI's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing.

input.rationale: This is a hosting agreement under which HDI operates the Site, holds Company Content and user information (Section 8.1) and generates order/export files (Section 1.5). Section 4 addresses only term, notice and the Termination Payment; Sections 8 and 10.7 impose confidentiality and survival but nowhere require HDI to return or delete the Company's data or to assist with migration after the Termination Date. No transition, exit or data-return language appears anywhere in the document, so the rule's preferred position is absent and we insert a new Section 4.3 covering up to six months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, machine-readable data return within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

content.text:
**Finding: missing (medium severity) — transition assistance and data return absent.**

**What I found.** This is a site development and hosting agreement where HDI holds materially all of our operational data: it stores and operates the Site (§1.4), generates order export files and processes our inventory imports (§1.5), and is expressly exposed to our "Content, user information, data, knowledge and proprietary and trade secret information" (§8.1).

Despite that, Section 4 (Term; Termination; Termination Payment) covers only the renewal/notice mechanics, the Termination Date, and our obligation to pay HDI a Termination Payment. There is no transition, exit, wind-down, migration, or data return/deletion language anywhere in the document — searches for "return" and "customer data" surfaced nothing on point, and §10.7 (Survival) preserves only §§6.3, 7, 9 and 10. Notably the asymmetry runs against us: we owe an eight-quarter Termination Payment on exit but get no contractual right to our own data back or any help standing the Site up elsewhere.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** Inserted a new Section 4.3 after §4.2(c), tracking the playbook's preferred position:

- (a) up to six (6) months of reasonable transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, including migration cooperation;
- (b) return of all Content, user information, customer data, order data and Confidential Information within thirty (30) days in a commonly used, machine-readable format;
- (c) deletion thereafter with written certification.

I placed it in Section 4 rather than creating a new section so the obligation sits with the existing termination mechanics and inherits the defined "Termination Date." The comment flags the fallback (90 days of assistance, same 30-day export) in case HDI pushes back on the six-month tail.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
This is a hosting agreement under which HDI operates the Site, holds Company Content and user information (Section 8.1) and generates order/export files (Section 1.5). Section 4 addresses only term, notice and the Termination Payment; Sections 8 and 10.7 impose confidentiality and survival but nowhere require HDI to return or delete the Company's data or to assist with migration after the Termination Date. No transition, exit or data-return language appears anywhere in the document, so the rule's preferred position is absent and we insert a new Section 4.3 covering up to six months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, machine-readable data return within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter.

Original paragraphs:
p0023: 4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.
p0024: 4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").
p0029: (c) The Termination Payment, if any, shall be payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments to be made quarterly, commencing thirty (30) days after the termination date.

Resolved definitions:
Company: This SITE DEVELOPMENT AND HOSTING AGREEMENT (the "Agreement") dated as of August 9, 1999 is made between Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI"), a New Jersey Corporation, located at 1500 Harbor Boulevard, Weehawken, NJ 07087, and The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (the "Company"), a Nevada corporation, located at 2500 Arrowhead Drive, Carson City, NV 89706. Each of the parties hereto shall be referred to as a "Party".
Termination Date: 4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").

Rendered redline:
p0029: (c) The Termination Payment, if any, shall be payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments to be made quarterly, commencing thirty (30) days after the termination date.
4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site and its operations to the Company or its designee; (b) within thirty (30) days after the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer data, order data and other Confidential Information of the Company then in HDI's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing.

Comment:
[Playbook] Section 4 sets out termination mechanics and the Termination Payment but says nothing about winding down the hosted Site, so we have added an exit clause requiring HDI to return the Company's Content, user, customer and order data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, provide up to six (6) months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, and certify deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety (90) days of assistance with the same thirty-day data export.

input.rationale: Fees under Section 3.1 are a pure revenue share (30% of monthly Net Sales above $11,000), so there is no minimum spend or purchase commitment on us. However, Section 4.2(a) imposes a volume-based Termination Payment (half of trailing 12-month Net Sales less $800,000) whenever the Company terminates, which operates as a penalty on our only exit route under Section 4.1 and applies even where we terminate because HDI has failed to perform. Because HDI bears all development and hosting costs, deleting the payment outright (preferred position) is disproportionate, so we took the fallback: keep the negotiated payment but carve out termination for HDI's material breach and termination under Section 1.6 (which already provides for termination "without penalty").

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity, fallback redline).**

**What I found**
- **No minimum purchase commitment.** Section 3.1 fees are a pure revenue share (30% of monthly Net Sales above $11,000), with no minimum spend, guaranteed volume, or shortfall mechanic. Section 6.1 restricts us competitively (exclusivity), but that is not a volume cap and falls outside this rule.
- **But Section 4.2(a) is a take-or-pay proxy on exit.** Our only exit under Section 4.1 is 90 days' notice; exercising it triggers a payment equal to half of trailing 12-month Net Sales less $800,000, payable in eight quarterly installments. It is volume-based, one-directional (only when *we* terminate), and applies even if we terminate because HDI failed to perform — a penalty rather than a true-up.

**Position taken**
Preferred (delete the payment) is disproportionate here: HDI bears all design, development, hosting and promotion costs (Sections 1.2, 1.6, 1.8) with no fixed fees from us, so the payment is a negotiated recoupment. I took the fallback with a single minimal insertion into Section 4.2(a) carving out (i) termination for HDI's material breach and (ii) termination under Section 1.6 — which already promises termination "without penalty," so that carve-out simply removes an internal inconsistency.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Fees under Section 3.1 are a pure revenue share (30% of monthly Net Sales above $11,000), so there is no minimum spend or purchase commitment on us. However, Section 4.2(a) imposes a volume-based Termination Payment (half of trailing 12-month Net Sales less $800,000) whenever the Company terminates, which operates as a penalty on our only exit route under Section 4.1 and applies even where we terminate because HDI has failed to perform. Because HDI bears all development and hosting costs, deleting the payment outright (preferred position) is disproportionate, so we took the fallback: keep the negotiated payment but carve out termination for HDI's material breach and termination under Section 1.6 (which already provides for termination "without penalty").

Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Because HDI funds the Site and the Deerskin-brand exclusivity is the core bargain, we took the fallback rather than outright deletion: the restriction is limited to a self-contained "Deerskin" branded consumer web site, remains term-only (Section 4.1 term is one year with annual renewals terminable on 90 days' notice, so no post-term tail), and carve-outs for other channels, internal development and acquisitions are added.","proposal":"Narrow Section 6.1 exclusivity so it binds the Company only as to a Deerskin-branded Site, with carve-outs for other channels, internal development and acquisitions","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-b313075d","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 4.1 gives the Company no mid-term convenience exit (only a 90-day notice tied to the annual renewal) while granting HDI a mirror-image 90-day right that on its face could be exercised mid-term, contrary to our position that the Vendor may not walk away during a committed term. It names only "the Company", so our affiliates and the contractors who would operate and monitor the Site on our behalf are outside the grant, and nothing prevents HDI from revoking or suspending the access at will or on a change of control. That falls short of the playbook position that the licence extend to affiliates and contractors and not be revocable at the vendor's discretion. The licence we grant HDI in the "Deerskin" Marks (§6.1) is already non-exclusive, non-transferable and limited to carrying out its obligations, so no change is needed there. Redline adds affiliate/contractor coverage plus non-revocability absent our uncured material breach and successor coverage; fallback is affiliate coverage on written notice and successor transfer only.","proposal":"Extend the §1.4 access/use grant to our affiliates and contractors, and make it non-revocable absent our uncured material breach, with successor coverage.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-6fe8a6db","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or best-terms obligation running against us. Consistent with the playbook, a Vendor-granted MFN-style benefit is welcome and is not redlined.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-bd15ed64","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Fees under Section 3.1 are a pure revenue share (30% of monthly Net Sales above $11,000), so there is no minimum spend or purchase commitment on us. Basis for absence: searches for each detection trigger ("solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "personnel") plus a sweep of every "shall not" obligation returned only three categories of text, none of which restricts hiring: (i) p0061, quoted above, where "employee" appears solely as a relationship descriptor in the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture clause; (ii) the confidentiality duties at p0048-p0054, which restrict use and disclosure of information, not recruitment of staff; and (iii) the Section 6 exclusivity covenants, which restrict participation in competing Internet projects for Deerskin Products (p0037 binding the Company, p0042 binding HDI) rather than solicitation or hiring of either party's employees.

Party mapping: our client, The Deerskin Companies, Inc. ("the Company"), is the customer under this site development and hosting agreement; HDI is the vendor/host. The rule's concern is a covenant binding Customer, and none exists.

On the outstanding "general-solicitation carve-out" check: this is not a defect and cannot be cured. The check tests an attribute that can only exist inside a non-solicit clause, as does the companion 12-month duration check. With no such clause in the document, there is no duration to shorten and no carve-out to attach. Drafting a carve-out would require first drafting the restrictive covenant it qualifies, importing a personnel restriction on us that the counterparty never sought and moving us away from the preferred position. The correct outcome is therefore no edit, and the rendered paragraphs remain byte-identical to the originals.

Separate note for the deal team, outside NOSOLICIT scope: the exclusivity covenant at p0037 does bind us during the term, and is asymmetric in our favour only as to duration - HDI's mirror covenant at p0042 runs for the term plus two years and survives under Section 10.7, while ours is term-only. That competition restriction should be reviewed under the applicable exclusivity/non-compete rule.","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-renewal-04a745d4","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"Section 4.1 provides automatic one-year renewals (renewal term length is acceptable), but the exit notice window is ninety (90) days — three times our preferred 30-day window and beyond the 60-day fallback, sitting at the walk-away boundary. There is also no pre-renewal reminder from HDI. Fees are a fixed 30% revenue share under Section 3.1 with no uplift mechanism, so no price-increase cap is required. Redline shortens our notice to 30 days (leaving HDI's notice at 90 days so we retain longer runway) and adds a 60-day renewal reminder from HDI; 60 days for our notice is an acceptable fallback.","proposal":"Shorten the Company's non-renewal/termination notice to 30 days and require a 60-day renewal reminder from HDI","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-1a29e6eb","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and","rationale":"This is a hosting agreement under which HDI operates the Site, holds Company Content and user information (Section 8.1) and generates order/export files (Section 1.5). Section 4 addresses only term, notice and the Termination Payment; Sections 8 and 10.7 impose confidentiality and survival but nowhere require HDI to return or delete the Company's data or to assist with migration after the Termination Date. No transition, exit or data-return language appears anywhere in the document, so the rule's preferred position is absent and we insert a new Section 4.3 covering up to six months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, machine-readable data return within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter.","proposal":"Insert Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide transition assistance, return Company data in machine-readable format within 30 days, and certify deletion.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-a6248bb3","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"Section 9 is limited to mutual corporate authority representations (p0056–p0057) plus a Globix carve-out (p0058); there is no express warranty that HDI's site development and hosting Services will be performed in a workmanlike manner, that the Site will conform to the approved specifications, or any repair/re-performance/refund remedy. Sections 1 and 5 impose delivery and operational obligations on HDI but no quality warranty (the only quality-adjacent right is termination if the Site is not operational within 70 days, p0011). There is no "AS IS" or implied-warranty disclaimer, so inserting the express warranty does not require a disclaimer carve-out. We therefore insert a new Section 9(c) with the preferred warranty package (workmanlike Services, 12-month Site conformance, legal compliance, no malicious code) and a repair/re-performance/refund remedy, noting the 90/30-day fallback.","proposal":"Add an HDI performance warranty for the Site and hosting Services, with a repair/re-performance/refund remedy.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-insurance-9eb3be7c","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a","rationale":"The Agreement contains no insurance provision anywhere (no hits for "insurance"; General Provisions in Section 10 run from notices to headings/counterparts). HDI designs, hosts and operates the Site on its own servers and has access to our Confidential Information, Content and Site user information (Sections 1.1, 1.3, 8.1), so the playbook requires standard vendor coverage. Added a new Section 10.9 in the miscellaneous section with CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, plus certificates on request; fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M flagged in the comment.","proposal":"Insert vendor insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' comp) as new Section 10.9","verification":"pass"}]

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (Site Development and Hosting Agreement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the HDI Site Development and Hosting Agreement — verified findings only

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. HDI is the vendor: it designs, develops, hosts, operates and promotes the Site and performs "Services" for us, yet the Agreement is silent on the three protections we treat as non-negotiable. There is **no indemnification** of any kind, **no limitation of liability or damages exclusion**, and **no IP ownership or data-ownership provision** — meaning we fund the Site through a revenue share and a Termination Payment without confirmed ownership of the deliverables, our Content or the customer data, and with unlimited mutual exposure. We propose a vendor indemnity (new § 9(c)), a mutual cap with uncapped Excluded Claims (new § 10.9), and an ownership section.

The second cluster of issues is the exit economics. Section 4.2(a) imposes a Termination Payment of 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 on *any* termination by us — including termination for HDI's own non-performance — against fees of only 30% of Net Sales. Combined with § 6.1's exclusive dealing covenant (Deerskin Products and "substantially similar" products, sweeping in third-party competitor lines) and § 4.1's 90-day, renewal-only notice window, we are effectively locked in for the full term with no performance-based exit. We have taken playbook fallbacks rather than outright deletion, recognising that HDI funds the build, hosting and promotion.

Remaining items are more contained: HDI's uncapped inspection right (§ 3.4), the missing venue designation under the otherwise-acceptable New York governing law clause (§ 10.5), the narrow § 1.4 access grant, the absence of transition assistance and data return, the absence of a performance warranty, and the absence of vendor insurance. Two points are already compliant or require no edit: there is no MFN burdening us (and § 1.8's "no less favorably" promotion covenant runs in our favour), and there is no non-solicit binding us — though that finding did not pass verification and should be re-run before we rely on it.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 (insertion point: new § 9(c)) | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language anywhere; § 7.2 is a covenant only. Add HDI indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, HDI-caused data incidents and misconduct, carving out Company-provided Content and Marks. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | Preamble / Agreement-wide | No ownership or assignment provision; § 10.2 is a partnership carve-out, not an IP allocation. Add: Company owns Site deliverables, Content, Marks and customer data; HDI retains its platform with a perpetual licence back; no joint ownership. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Missing | § 5.4 (insertion point: new § 10.9) | No cap, no damages exclusion; unlimited direct and consequential exposure both ways. Add mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' § 3 fees or USD 1,000,000, mutual consequential-damages exclusion, uncapped Excluded Claims, and confirmation that our payment/Termination Payment obligations are not "damages". |
| 4 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 1.4 (operative: §§ 4.1, 4.2(a)) | No mid-term convenience exit for us; HDI's mirror 90-day right could be exercised mid-term; § 4.2(a) penalty applies even on our termination for HDI's fault. Add 30-day Company convenience right with refund of prepaid fees, confine HDI's convenience right to end-of-term non-renewal, cap the Termination Payment at three months' fees with a fault-based carve-out. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (operative: § 4.2) | Termination Payment is uncapped, unrelated to fees payable, and triggered by any termination by us. Fallback taken: single early-termination fee capped at three months' § 3.1 fees, payable only on termination for convenience and not under § 1.6 or for HDI's breach. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 (operative: § 6.1) | Exclusive dealing for the full auto-renewing term with no performance-based exit — our walk-away position. Fallback taken: confine to Deerskin Products for a fixed 12 months, terminating automatically on HDI's failure to meet service levels, availability requirements or delivery dates (including the § 1.6 launch date). HDI's reciprocal covenant (§ 6.3) and the § 6.2 closeout carve-out are left untouched. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 (operative: § 6.1) | Field-of-use restriction extends to "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products," expressly sweeping in third-party competitor lines, with no carve-out for internal development or acquired businesses. Fallback taken: limit to a self-contained "Deerskin"-branded consumer web site, term-only, with carve-outs for other channels, internal development and acquisitions. |
| 8 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 5.4 (operative: § 10.3) | Bare successors-and-assigns clause: no customer affiliate/successor carve-out, no restriction on HDI assigning (including to a Deerskin competitor), no change-of-control provision. Add affiliate/successor carve-out for us, consent standard on HDI (not unreasonably withheld, never to a competitor), and confirmation that our change of control is not an assignment and gives HDI no exit. |
| 9 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 1.4 (operative: § 4.1) | One-year renewal length is acceptable, but the 90-day exit notice is three times our preferred window and beyond the 60-day fallback. Shorten our notice to 30 days (leaving HDI's at 90 days) and add a 60-day renewal reminder from HDI; 60 days for our notice is acceptable. No price-increase cap needed (fixed 30% revenue share). |
| 10 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Deviation | § 1.4 (operative: § 4.2(a)) | No minimum spend (fees are a pure revenue share), but the volume-based Termination Payment penalises our only exit route. Fallback taken: keep the negotiated payment but carve out termination for HDI's material breach and termination under § 1.6 (which already contemplates termination "without penalty"). |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Missing | § 5.4 (insertion point: new § 9(c)) | § 9 is limited to mutual corporate authority representations plus a Globix carve-out; no workmanlike-services, conformance or remedy provision. Add workmanlike Services, 12-month Site conformance, legal compliance and no-malicious-code warranties with a repair/re-performance/refund remedy (90/30-day fallback noted). No "AS IS" disclaimer to displace. |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 1.4 (insertion point: new § 4.3) | HDI holds our Content, user information and order/export files, but nothing requires return, deletion or migration assistance. Insert up to six months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, machine-readable data return within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. |
| 13 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 | The only grant in our favour names "the Company" alone, excluding affiliates and the contractors who would operate the Site, and is revocable at will. Extend to affiliates and contractors, make it non-revocable absent our uncured material breach, and add successor coverage (fallback: affiliate coverage on written notice plus successor transfer). The Marks licence we grant HDI (§ 6.1) needs no change. |
| 14 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (operative: § 3.4) | HDI's inspection right already gives 30 days' notice, business hours and HDI-borne costs, but is unlimited in frequency with no confidentiality requirement and no systems carve-out. Cap at once per 12 months, require an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, off-site where practicable, and bar direct or remote system access. We deliberately omit the >5% cost-shift, as unconditional HDI cost allocation is better for us. |
| 15 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 5.4 (operative: § 10.5) | New York law is our preferred choice and there is no arbitration or foreign venue provision, but no forum is specified. Add exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, leaving the governing law wording untouched. |
| 16 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 (insertion point: new § 10.9) | No insurance provision anywhere, despite HDI hosting on its own servers with access to our Confidential Information, Content and Site user information. Add CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request (fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). |
| 17 | Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 1.4 (§§ 3.1–3.4, § 1.8) | No MFN or best-terms obligation runs against us; § 6.1 is an exclusivity covenant, not an MFN. § 1.8's "no less favorably" promotion covenant runs in our favour and is not redlined. No action. |
| 18 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 5.4 | Finding records no non-solicit, no-hire or inducement covenant anywhere, so the preferred position is met and no edit is proposed. **Verification did not pass** — re-run before relying on this conclusion. |

We propose a vendor indemnity (new § 9(c)), a mutual cap with uncapped Excluded Claims (new § 10.9), and an ownership section.

The second cluster of issues is the exit economics. Section 4.2(a) imposes a Termination Payment of 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 on *any* termination by us — including termination for HDI's own non-performance — against fees of only 30% of Net Sales.
